packet_ingest.dedupe_rule: Historical pre-execution enforcement is credited once; current stern nonblocking bookkeeping/per-call identity findings are referenced but not re-credited because dedicated current-effect deltas already exist.

architecture_findings.finding: Project-Frankenstein AgentLoop/ToolExecutor implemented genuine pre-execution denial: risky calls waited for user approval and a denied or timed-out approval did not call ToolExecutor.execute for that action.

The approval handshake was not structurally consumed by the execution boundary. request_approval created an approval_id keyed to tool_name/tool_input, but the later execute() call accepted only tool_name, tool_input and caller-controlled skip_approval; approval_id, approved request digest, generation and immutable invocation identity were not arguments to execute().

Both fixed-name safe auto-approval and the human-approved risky path converged on execute(..., skip_approval=True). Therefore the final executor trusted caller discipline instead of independently validating a typed, exact-call decision token.

The historical approval queue persisted full tool_input in JSON. Frankenstein 2.0 must not copy this representation into canonical effect/approval journals; secrets and bulky payloads need typed minimal metadata plus digest/reference boundaries.

The historical and current lineages contain complementary halves rather than one monotonic EffectGate: the historical path had real pre-execution deny but weak exact-decision binding; current stern has richer generation/idempotency/outcome journaling but ordinary admission is intentionally nonblocking. Frankenstein 2.0 should fuse the strengths without inheriting either weakness.

frankenstein_2_effect_decision_binding.human_approval_rule: Human approval is evidence/input to deterministic EffectGate policy for one exact request; it is not a reusable boolean bypass and does not itself mutate canonical state.
frankenstein_2_effect_decision_binding.executor_rule: The actual executor boundary must validate that the decision identity, request digest, generation and invocation identity match the exact request immediately before dispatch. ALLOW is consumed/marked for that invocation according to the effect protocol; stale, mismatched, replayed or absent decisions fail closed.
frankenstein_2_effect_decision_binding.no_retroactive_authority: A later successful execution receipt cannot create or repair a missing ALLOW decision retroactively.
frankenstein_2_effect_decision_binding.payload_rule: Persist typed minimal metadata and hashes/references; redact secrets before persistence; raw tool_input is not default durable approval/effect material.

required_triggerword4_acceptance_tests: Approve request A, then mutate any decision-relevant argument before execution: executor must reject the request-digest mismatch.
Replay one consumed/closed ALLOW decision for a second invocation with the same tool name and arguments: reject by invocation identity/replay state.
Use an ALLOW decision from another session or generation: reject before dispatch.
DENY or ADMISSION_UNKNOWN: prove zero effect dispatch, not merely a denial journal row.
Human approval times out or response is missing: remain non-ALLOW and do not execute through a skip-approval fallback.
Parallel approvals for two calls complete in reverse order: each decision remains bound to the correct invocation and request digest.
Secret-fence: representative keys/tokens/passwords in tool arguments never appear in approval/effect durable rows; allowed digests/references remain sufficient to correlate the exact request.
Successful post-execution outcome without a matching prior decision remains execution evidence only and cannot satisfy admission/completion authority.
preserved_counterhypotheses: A historical overlay or wrapper outside the inspected files may have revalidated approved request contents or consumed approvals one-shot before execution; no such invariant is established by the examined source.

If historical AgentLoop was the only caller and runtime was strictly serialized, caller discipline could have reduced practical mismatch frequency; that still does not establish a reusable exact authority contract.
The separately referenced wache-koenig predecessor may bridge part of the enforcement lineage; its exact source and runtime order remain unproven.

contradictions.claim_a: Historical AgentLoop/ToolExecutor could actually prevent a risky call before execution.
contradictions.claim_b: The final execute() boundary did not consume the approval_id or exact approved-request digest and accepted a caller-controlled skip_approval flag.
contradictions.resolution: Retain pre-execution enforcement as donor value; replace the loose approval-to-execute bridge with immutable exact-request EffectDecision binding.
